messages:
ops-bot: [ALERT] nvml_thermal_event spike detected on 8 nodes in pool-gpu-usw2. hosts: gpu-021,gpu-022,gpu-023,gpu-024,gpu-043,gpu-044,gpu-045,gpu-046. metric: GPU_TEMP > 90C repeatedly, XidCount incrementing. Auto-evict policy currently ignores thermal-only signals. link: https://telemetry.internal/redwood/alerts/1768804321

maria_dev: seeing the same. nodes in k8s cluster 'infer-usw2'. multiple infer pods on those nodes. no automatic cordon occurred.

chen_infra: quick question — is thermal supposed to trigger cordon after N spikes? policy doc says cordon on 3 consecutive NVML thermal events within 10m, but operator uses "5 XID or ECC" for full drain. thermal-only path was never fully implemented.

raj_sre: we built a "soft-evict" flow (cordon + notify) for transient thermal issues. sounds like webhook didn't fire. checking operator logs now.

lisa_ml: this matches latency anomalies we've seen. token p95 for some batches jumped ~2.3x while these nodes were active. if we drain 8 nodes at once we risk capacity shortfall for high-priority customers. :grimacing:

sam: idea: stagger drains. annotate node with redwood.io/evict-delay and perform cordon-first, then drain only if persistent. Also route batch jobs to slurm-preempt group while interactive keeps priority.

chen_infra: operator logs show webhook timeouts to /internal/healthhook: 504 gateway from infra-proxy. root cause: PD flood (lots of P1s) causing our request queue to back up. the thermal watcher attempted to escalate but hit the timeout.

maria_dev: can we change the default behavior to cordon-only on thermal events and not attempt immediate full drain? cordon reduces risk and lets autoscaler handle replacement windows.

raj_sre: +1. propose workflow: 1) cordon + restart GPU daemon (nvidia-device-plugin) -> clear transient stuck states, 2) wait 15m (2 telemetry cycles), 3) if nvml events persist or Xid increases -> drain and migrate pods, 4) if still flaky -> mark node for replacement/provisioning with tag 'thermal_flaky'.

sam: cordon script prototype attached below. it's intentionally conservative so we don't cascade evictions across pools.

sam: ```bash
NODE=$1
kubectl annotate node $NODE redwood.io/evict-mode=cordon --overwrite
kubectl cordon $NODE
# wait 15 minutes for telemetry to stabilize
sleep 900
# re-check via telemetry API
curl -s "https://telemetry.internal/api/v1/nodes/$NODE/metrics?metric=nvml_thermal_count" | jq .
# if count > 0 -> kubectl drain --delete-local-data --ignore-daemonsets $NODE
```

lisa_ml: ops constraint: please gate automatic replacement behind a utilization check. don't spin up dedicated replacements unless cluster util < 80% and degradation persisted > 30m, otherwise we blow committed capacity.

chen_infra: created PR 1427: adds cordon-first logic, webhook retry/backoff (exponential), and evict-delay annotation support. will deploy to staging tonight and roll to prod in canary waves.

maria_dev: thanks. can someone add a Grafana panel for 'thermal-cordons' vs 'full-drains' per week so we can measure regressions after this change? also add an alert if cordons spike > 5/day.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-3482 created for thermal spike cascade. assignees: @chen_infra @raj_sre. Current status: investigating. (update ts: 1768807921)
